'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Southern Ukraine campaign]]
***[[Russia]] says that it destroyed the [[Ukrainian Navy]] warship [[Ukrainian ship Yuri Olefirenko|''Yuri Olefirenko'']] at the [[Port of Odesa]] in a [[missile]] strike on May 29. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-says-it-destroys-ukraines-last-warship-2023-05-31/ (Reuters)]
**[[2022–2023 Western Russia attacks]]
***Russian authorities say that a [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[drone warfare|drone strike]] has caused a fire at an [[oil refinery]] in [[Krasnodar Krai]], and also caused damage in [[Shebekino]], [[Belgorod Oblast]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukrainian-drone-sparks-fire-russian-refinery-governor-2023-05-31/ (Reuters)]
**[[Battle of Donbas (2022–present)|Battle of Donbas]]
***According to Russian authorities, five people are killed and 19 others are injured by Ukrainian [[shell (projectile)|shelling]] in Karpaty, in Russian-occupied [[Luhansk Oblast]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2023-05-31/five-dead-in-ukraine-shelling-of-luhansk-village-moscow-installed-centre (US News)]
*[[Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso]]
**About 100 gunmen [[ambush]] a military escort of a food convoy in Tibou, killing two civilians. At least 50 of the attackers are killed in the ensuing [[Shootout|gunfight]] with [[Burkina Faso Armed Forces|soldiers]]. [https://www.africanews.com/amp/2023/06/02/burkina-2-civilians-and-50-terrorists-killed-in-an-attack-in-the-north/ (Africa News)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**Five members of the [[Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine – General Command]] are killed and ten others are injured in an explosion at a base in Qusaya, [[Beqaa Governorate]], [[Lebanon]]. The PFLP accuses the [[Israel Defense Forces]] of responsibility. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2023/5/31/5-palestinian-fighters-killed-in-lebanon-blast-blamed-on-israel (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2022–2023 North Kosovo crisis]]
**[[NATO]] deploys a further 700 troops to [[North Kosovo]] to reinforce its [[Kosovo Force|KFOR]] [[peacekeeping]] mission amid clashes with [[Kosovo Serbs|Kosovo Serb]] protesters over the election and installation of [[Kosovo Albanians|ethnic Albanian]] mayors in several Serb-majority towns following a Serbian election boycott. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/us-troops-guard-town-hall-northern-kosovo-2023-05-31/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The tapes for a long lost, unreleased [[John Coltrane]] live album with [[Eric Dolphy]] are found at the [[New York Public Library for the Performing Arts]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/music/2023/jun/01/john-coltrane-recordings-lost-in-new-york-public-library-will-finally-be-heard (''The Guardian'')]
*Tito Sotto, Vic Sotto, and Joey de Leon announces their departure from ''Eat Bulaga!'' and TAPE Inc. that produced for nearly 44 years in the Philippines. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/entertainment/05/31/23/tito-vic-and-joey-announce-departure-from-tape-inc (''ABS-CBN News'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Cannich wildfire]]
**A [[wildfire]] which had been burning for four days in the [[Scottish Highlands]] is brought under control after affecting about {{cvt|30|sqmi}} of land, making it the largest ever recorded in the [[United Kingdom]]. ([https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-highlands-islands-65765053 BBC News])
*A magnitude 5.9 earthquake strikes [[Kachin State]], [[Myanmar]], with damage reported. [https://latestnews.fresherslive.com/articles/buildings-damaged-during-earthquake-in-myanmar-1347826 (Fresherslive)]

'''International relations'''
*The [[United Arab Emirates]] confirms that it has withdrawn from the [[United States Navy]]-led [[Combined Task Force 150]] mission in the [[Persian Gulf]] amid recent seizures of [[oil tanker]]s by [[Iran]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/uae-says-it-withdrew-us-led-maritime-coalition-two-months-ago-2023-05-31/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2023 Bournemouth beach incident]]
**Two people die and eight others are injured during an incident at a beach in [[Bournemouth]], [[Dorset]], [[United Kingdom]]. A man has been arrested on suspicion of [[manslaughter]], according to [[Dorset Police]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-dorset-65771464 (BBC News)]
*The [[Kyrgyzstan]] [[Prosecutor General's Office of Kyrgyzstan|Prosecutor-General's Office]] calls for lawmakers to allow the prosecution of [[United Kyrgyzstan]] opposition leader [[Adakhan Madumarov]] for alleged attempts to seize power. [https://www.rferl.org/amp/kyrgyz-prosecutor-general-opposition-leader/32437533.html (RFE/RL)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Australian Indigenous Voice referendum]]
**The ''Constitution Alteration (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Voice) 2023'' bill passes the [[Australian House of Representatives]], thereby allowing for a [[Referendums in Australia|referendum]] on an [[Indigenous Voice to Parliament]] later this year. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-05-31/voice-to-parliament-referendum-bill-passes-the-lower-house/102414444 (ABC News Australia)]
*[[2023 Latvian presidential election]]
**[[Edgars Rinkēvičs]] is elected the 11th [[President of Latvia]]. [https://eng.lsm.lv/article/politics/president/31.05.2023-edgars-rinkevics-elected-president-of-latvia.a510815/ (LSM)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**In a news release published by [[NASA]], it is revealed that the [[James Webb Space Telescope]] has discovered traces of water on the [[exoplanet]] [[WASP-18b]], which has a mass equal to 10 [[Jupiter mass|Jupiters]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/webb-telescope-discovers-traces-of-water-in-atmosphere-of-exoplanet-with-mass-of-10-jupiters/ (CBS News)]
*The launch of the [[North Korea|North Korean]] spy satellite ''[[Malligyong-1]]'' ends in failure due to a malfunction of the second stage of the rocket, causing the satellite to crash into the sea. An [[emergency evacuation]] alert was erroneously sent to residents of [[Seoul]], [[South Korea]], after the rocket launch, which also triggered [[civil defense siren|air raid siren]]s in the city. [https://apnews.com/article/north-korea-launch-military-spy-satellite-db6ce3f08e1ec8e23674aef519d04403 (AP)] [https://www.ft.com/content/ba838cdf-a1df-451f-a153-5972050b3634 (''Financial Times'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022–23 UEFA Europa League]]
**In [[association football]], [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] win a [[UEFA Cup and Europa League records and statistics|record-extending]] seventh [[UEFA Europa League]] title after defeating [[A.S. Roma]] 4–1 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] following a 1–1 draw after [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]] in the [[2023 UEFA Europa League final]] at the [[Puskás Aréna]] in [[Budapest]], [[Hungary]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2023/may/31/sevilla-v-roma-europa-league-final-live (''The Guardian'')]
